title: Surgical safety checklist (WHO)
definition: WHO 3-phase checklist to reduce perioperative complications: Sign In (pre-anesthesia), Time Out (pre-incision), Sign Out (pre-leaving OT).
keyPoints: Sign In: patient identity, site marked, allergies, airway risk, blood loss risk >500 mL
Time Out: whole team introductions, confirm surgery + site, antibiotic within 60 min, imaging available
Sign Out: procedure recorded, instrument/sponge count, specimen labeled, concerns for recovery
pearls: Time Out done immediately before skin incision.
clinicalContext: 28-y-old about to undergo appendectomy; team paused before incision.
nursingPriority: Lead Time Out: verbal confirmation of patient, procedure, site, antibiotic prophylaxis given, imaging displayed.

title: Patient positions — surgical
definition: Positions on OT table for surgical access.
keyPoints: Supine: most surgeries
Trendelenburg: pelvic surgery — venous return risk
Reverse Trendelenburg: head/neck, laparoscopic upper abdomen
Lithotomy: perineal, vaginal — nerve injury risk (peroneal)
Prone/Jackknife: spine, perianal
Lateral/Sims: kidney, chest
Fowler: neurosurgery — air embolism risk
pearls: Lithotomy >2 h increases peroneal/sciatic injury risk.
clinicalContext: Patient for hemorrhoidectomy positioned on OT table.
nursingPriority: Place in jackknife (prone with hips flexed 90°), pad pressure points, secure with straps, check ventilation.

title: OT positions
definition: Standardized operating team positions around the table.
keyPoints: Surgeon: right of patient (for right-handed)
Assistant: opposite surgeon
Scrub nurse: foot end or right of surgeon
Anesthetist: head end
Circulator: periphery, coordinates supplies
clinicalContext: Setting up for open cholecystectomy.
nursingPriority: Position surgeon on patient right, scrub nurse adjacent, instrument trolley between; anesthetist at head.

title: Cautery — mono vs bi-polar
definition: Electrosurgery for cutting/coagulation using high-frequency current.
keyPoints: Monopolar: current from active electrode → ground pad; higher power; risk of burns if pad poor contact
Bipolar: current between 2 tips of forceps; safer near nerves/pacemakers; less collateral damage
Contraindicated absolute: flammable preps not dry
Check pad on dry well-vascularized area (thigh, back)
clinicalContext: Pacemaker patient for lap chole.
nursingPriority: Use bipolar cautery, apply ground pad on clean dry muscle, short bursts, liaise with cardiology to reprogram pacemaker to asynchronous mode.

title: Sutures and knots
definition: Materials for tissue approximation.
keyPoints: Absorbable: catgut (30 d), vicryl/polyglactin (56-70 d), monocryl (90-120 d), PDS (180 d)
Non-absorbable: silk, nylon, prolene, stainless steel
Size: smaller number = thicker (0 thicker than 3-0)
Surgeon knot: double throw first to reduce slippage
Skin closure: 3-0/4-0 nylon/monocryl subcuticular
clinicalContext: Closing skin on a clean abdominal wound.
nursingPriority: Use 3-0 monocryl subcuticular or 3-0 nylon interrupted, aseptic technique, document count.

title: Surgical site infection and prevention
definition: Infection at operative site within 30 d (or 1 y if implant).
keyPoints: Classes: superficial incisional, deep, organ/space
Prevention: skin antisepsis (CHG-alcohol), hair clipping not shaving, prophylactic antibiotic within 60 min, normothermia, glucose control (<200), sterile draping
Most common: S aureus; MRSA if risk factors
Remove drains as early as clinically safe
pearls: Cefazolin 2 g IV within 60 min before skin incision.
clinicalContext: Post-op day 4 colectomy patient with wound erythema, warm, purulent drainage.
nursingPriority: Collect pus swab for culture, obtain surgical review for drainage, start empiric antibiotic, document vitals, isolate if MRSA suspected.

title: Types of wound
definition: Wound classification for healing and infection risk.
keyPoints: Clean (I): no inflammation, GI/respiratory not entered; infection <2%
Clean-contaminated (II): controlled entry; 5-10%
Contaminated (III): fresh trauma, spillage; 15-20%
Dirty (IV): existing infection, perforated viscus; >30%
By healing: primary (sutured), secondary (granulation), tertiary (delayed primary)
clinicalContext: Perforated appendicitis with pus.
nursingPriority: Classify as dirty (IV); leave skin open for delayed primary closure, broad-spectrum antibiotics, irrigate peritoneum.

topic: Nutrition — NG tube feeding and TPN, CVP care
title: Nutrition — NG tube feeding and TPN, CVP care
definition: Enteral and parenteral nutrition routes and care.
keyPoints: NG tube: verify placement by pH <5.5 aspirate or X-ray; flush 30 mL water before/after feeds; HOB >=30°
TPN: central line, aseptic connections, monitor glucose q4-6h, gradual taper to prevent rebound hypoglycemia
CVP normal 2-8 mmHg; measure with patient supine, zero at phlebostatic axis (4th ICS mid-axillary)
Refeeding syndrome: watch phosphate, magnesium, potassium in chronically malnourished
pearls: If feeding intolerance: hold, reposition, recheck residual.
clinicalContext: Post-op patient on TPN via right IJ.
nursingPriority: Maintain aseptic technique at hub, monitor glucose q6h, daily dressing, flush with heparinized saline per protocol, watch for refeeding.

title: Shock — types and management
definition: Inadequate tissue perfusion and oxygenation.
keyPoints: Hypovolemic: hemorrhage, burns — replace volume
Cardiogenic: MI, arrhythmia — inotropes
Distributive: sepsis, anaphylaxis, neurogenic — vasopressors
Obstructive: PE, tamponade, tension pneumothorax — relieve obstruction
Early signs: tachycardia, cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure, oliguria
clinicalContext: 30-y-old MVA, BP 70/40, HR 140, cool clammy, abdomen tender.
nursingPriority: Two large-bore IVs, crystalloid 1 L bolus, cross-match 4 units, FAST scan, urinary catheter, prepare for emergency laparotomy.

title: Basics of trauma
definition: Systematic ATLS primary survey.
keyPoints: A: Airway with C-spine control
B: Breathing (look, listen, feel; tension pneumothorax)
C: Circulation (control bleeding, 2 large IVs)
D: Disability (GCS, pupils)
E: Exposure + prevent hypothermia
Then secondary survey head-to-toe
clinicalContext: Multi-trauma from road accident.
nursingPriority: Simultaneous primary survey; cervical collar, high-flow O2, 2 large-bore IVs with warmed crystalloid, cover to prevent hypothermia, FAST.

title: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
definition: Bedside measure of consciousness: Eye + Verbal + Motor; range 3-15.
keyPoints: Eye: 4 spontaneous, 3 to speech, 2 to pain, 1 none
Verbal: 5 oriented, 4 confused, 3 inappropriate, 2 incomprehensible, 1 none
Motor: 6 obeys, 5 localizes, 4 withdraws, 3 flexion (decorticate), 2 extension (decerebrate), 1 none
GCS <=8 = coma, intubate
clinicalContext: Head injury patient opens eyes to pain, confused words, localizes pain.
nursingPriority: Calculate E2 V4 M5 = GCS 11 (moderate head injury); document, repeat q15 min, prepare CT scan.

title: Abdominal trauma
definition: Blunt or penetrating abdominal injury.
keyPoints: Blunt: spleen most common injured
Penetrating: liver most common
FAST scan: 4 windows — perihepatic, perisplenic, pelvis, pericardial
DPL positive if >10 mL blood or >100,000 RBC/mm3
Unstable + positive FAST → laparotomy
clinicalContext: Cyclist hit car, LUQ pain, BP 92/60.
nursingPriority: FAST scan; if positive + unstable, emergency laparotomy — likely splenic injury.

title: Thoracic trauma — pneumothorax and hemothorax
definition: Air (pneumo) or blood (hemo) in pleural space.
keyPoints: Tension pneumothorax: hyper-resonance, tracheal deviation, distended neck veins, shock — needle decompression 2nd ICS MCL (or 5th ICS AAL per ATLS 10e)
Open pneumothorax: 3-sided dressing
Massive hemothorax: >1500 mL initial or >200 mL/h — thoracotomy
Simple pneumo/hemo: chest tube 5th ICS AAL
pearls: Do not wait for X-ray in tension pneumothorax.
clinicalContext: Stabbing patient, absent breath sounds left, trachea deviated right, BP 80/50.
nursingPriority: Immediate needle decompression at 2nd ICS MCL left, prepare for chest tube insertion, high-flow O2.

title: Head injury — EDH and SDH
definition: Traumatic intracranial hemorrhage.
keyPoints: EDH: middle meningeal artery tear; biconvex/lens-shaped; lucid interval; 90% skull fracture
SDH: bridging vein rupture; crescent-shaped; elderly, alcoholics, anticoagulants; slower onset
Cushing triad (raised ICP): HTN + bradycardia + irregular respiration
Management: head up 30°, mannitol 0.25-1 g/kg, hyperventilation transient, craniotomy
clinicalContext: Young adult after fall, lucid then unconscious, pupil dilated on same side.
nursingPriority: Prepare for urgent non-contrast CT, maintain airway, head up 30°, notify neurosurgery — classic EDH presentation.

title: Burns — classification and management
definition: Thermal, chemical, or electrical skin injury.
keyPoints: Depth: superficial (epidermis), superficial partial (blisters, painful), deep partial (reduced sensation), full thickness (painless, leathery)
Rule of 9s adult: head 9, each arm 9, each leg 18, trunk front 18, back 18, genitalia 1
Pediatric Lund-Browder
Parkland formula: 4 mL x kg x %TBSA; half in first 8 h from injury, half in next 16 h
Refer if >10% TBSA, face/hands/perineum, full thickness
pearls: Urine output goal: adult 0.5 mL/kg/h, child 1 mL/kg/h.
clinicalContext: 70 kg adult, 30% TBSA full-thickness burn from kitchen fire 1 h ago.
nursingPriority: Secure airway, IV lactated Ringer 4x70x30 = 8400 mL (4200 first 8 h from burn time), Foley catheter, warm environment, tetanus.

topic: Plastic surgery — skin graft, Humbys knife
title: Plastic surgery — skin graft, Humbys knife
definition: Reconstructive skin coverage.
keyPoints: Split-thickness skin graft (STSG): epidermis + partial dermis; harvested with Humby knife or dermatome
Full-thickness graft (FTSG): better cosmesis, smaller area
Donor site heals 10-14 d
Graft take: 5-7 d; assess color, adherence
Stevens-Johnson, necrotizing fasciitis post-burn needs grafting
clinicalContext: Post burn debridement wound 10x15 cm requiring cover.
nursingPriority: Prepare donor site (thigh), harvest STSG with Humby knife, mesh for expansion, apply to wound with light pressure dressing.

title: Bedsores (pressure ulcer stages)
definition: NPUAP staging of pressure injuries.
keyPoints: Stage I: non-blanchable erythema, skin intact
Stage II: partial-thickness loss, blister
Stage III: full-thickness loss, visible fat
Stage IV: exposed bone/muscle/tendon
Unstageable: eschar-covered
Deep tissue injury: purple intact skin
Sites: sacrum, heels, ischium, greater trochanter, occiput
clinicalContext: Bedridden stroke patient with 2 cm non-blanchable erythema over sacrum.
nursingPriority: Stage I — offload sacrum with pillow, turn q2h, barrier cream, Braden assessment, hydrate, protein-rich diet.

title: Wound healing stages
definition: Phases of soft tissue repair.
keyPoints: Hemostasis (immediate): vasoconstriction, platelet plug, coagulation cascade
Inflammatory (0-5 d): neutrophils, macrophages
Proliferative (3-21 d): fibroblasts, angiogenesis, granulation, epithelialization
Maturation/remodeling (21 d to 1 y): collagen cross-linking, scar strengthens to ~80%
clinicalContext: Clean surgical wound day 7.
nursingPriority: Expect proliferative phase; remove sutures at 7-14 d per site, instruct on scar care.

title: Liver abscess and cancer
definition: Localized hepatic infection or malignancy.
keyPoints: Amoebic abscess: right lobe, anchovy-paste pus, PV travel; metronidazole + luminal agent
Pyogenic: polymicrobial; drain + broad-spectrum antibiotics
HCC: aflatoxin, HBV/HCV, cirrhosis; AFP >400 suggestive
Imaging: USG, triphasic CT
clinicalContext: Middle-aged man from rural area with RUQ pain, fever, hepatomegaly.
nursingPriority: USG — confirm amoebic abscess, start metronidazole 750 mg TDS x10 d + diloxanide, needle aspirate if large (>10 cm).

title: Gallbladder stones (cholelithiasis)
definition: Gallstones in gallbladder.
keyPoints: 5 F: Female, Fat, Fertile, Forty, Fair
Types: cholesterol (70%), pigment (hemolysis), mixed
Biliary colic: RUQ pain radiating to right shoulder, post-fatty meal
Cholecystitis: Murphy sign +, fever, leukocytosis
Treatment: laparoscopic cholecystectomy
clinicalContext: 45-y-old obese woman with severe RUQ pain post-meal, Murphy sign +.
nursingPriority: NPO, IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics if cholecystitis, prep for lap chole.

title: Pancreatitis and Whipple procedure
definition: Pancreas inflammation; Whipple for peri-ampullary cancer.
keyPoints: Acute: gallstone or alcohol, epigastric pain radiating to back, elevated lipase
Ranson score / APACHE II for severity
Grey-Turner (flank), Cullen (periumbilical) = hemorrhagic
Whipple: pancreaticoduodenectomy; removes head of pancreas, duodenum, CBD, gallbladder
clinicalContext: 50-y-old alcoholic with epigastric pain, lipase 1800, Ranson 4.
nursingPriority: NPO, IV fluids aggressively, pain control, NG if vomiting, monitor calcium, ICU for severe.

title: Renal stone and renal cancer
definition: Urolithiasis and RCC.
keyPoints: Stones: calcium oxalate (70%), struvite (infection), uric acid, cystine
Colic: loin to groin pain, hematuria, restless
Imaging: NCCT KUB gold standard
RCC: hematuria, flank pain, mass (classic triad rare); clear cell most common
Staging: T, N, M; nephrectomy for localized
clinicalContext: Patient writhing with right flank pain, hematuria.
nursingPriority: NCCT, analgesia (diclofenac IM), hydration, alpha-blocker tamsulosin for stones <10 mm, strain urine for stone analysis.

title: Horseshoe kidney
definition: Congenital fusion of lower poles of kidneys across midline.
keyPoints: Prevalence: 1 in 500
Isthmus usually trapped by IMA
Complications: UTI, stones, hydronephrosis
Usually asymptomatic; incidental imaging
clinicalContext: Incidental finding on CT abdomen.
nursingPriority: Reassure; monitor for UTI, stones; refer if obstruction.

title: Bladder cancer
definition: Most common urinary malignancy; transitional cell carcinoma >90%.
keyPoints: Risk: smoking (most important), aniline dye, schistosomiasis (squamous), chronic catheter
Painless gross hematuria most common symptom
Diagnosis: cystoscopy + biopsy
Treatment: TURBT, intravesical BCG for non-muscle invasive; cystectomy for invasive
clinicalContext: 65-y-old smoker with painless hematuria.
nursingPriority: Urology referral, urgent cystoscopy, counsel smoking cessation.

title: Urethral trauma
definition: Anterior (bulbar) or posterior (membranous) urethral injury.
keyPoints: Signs: blood at meatus, high-riding prostate (posterior), perineal hematoma
Do NOT catheterize
Retrograde urethrogram first
Suprapubic catheter if rupture confirmed
clinicalContext: Pelvic fracture patient with blood at meatus.
nursingPriority: Do not insert Foley; arrange retrograde urethrogram, prepare suprapubic catheter, consult urology.

title: Hypospadias
definition: Congenital urethral opening on ventral penis.
keyPoints: Classification: glandular, coronal, penile, penoscrotal, perineal
Associated: chordee, cryptorchidism
Do NOT circumcise — foreskin used for repair
Repair at 6-18 mo
clinicalContext: Newborn boy with urethral opening on ventral penile shaft.
nursingPriority: Counsel parents, refer to pediatric urology, avoid circumcision — foreskin needed for reconstruction.

title: Ectopia vesicae
definition: Bladder exstrophy — failure of closure of anterior abdominal wall and bladder.
keyPoints: Everted bladder mucosa visible
Associated: epispadias, pubic diastasis
Cover with plastic wrap at birth, avoid latex, reconstruction staged
clinicalContext: Newborn with open bladder on lower abdomen.
nursingPriority: Cover bladder with plastic wrap (not gauze — will adhere), NICU, prevent hypothermia, pediatric urology urgent.

title: Undescended testis
definition: Testis not in scrotum by 3 mo (unilateral) or earlier bilaterally.
keyPoints: Risk: infertility, malignancy (seminoma), torsion, inguinal hernia
Orchidopexy at 6-12 mo
Bilateral → karyotype, endocrine workup
Retractile vs true undescended
clinicalContext: 6-mo-old with empty right hemiscrotum.
nursingPriority: Refer to pediatric surgery for orchidopexy around 6-12 mo.

title: Testicular torsion
definition: Twisting of spermatic cord — surgical emergency.
keyPoints: Peak age: puberty
Sudden severe scrotal pain, elevated testis, absent cremasteric reflex, Prehn sign negative (no relief with elevation)
Doppler USG — absent flow
Manual detorsion (open book), surgical exploration within 6 h
clinicalContext: 15-y-old with sudden left testicular pain 3 h, elevated, swollen.
nursingPriority: Emergency scrotal exploration within 6 h for salvage, avoid delays for imaging if classic.

title: Hernia — types and complications
definition: Protrusion of viscera through defect in containing wall.
keyPoints: Inguinal: direct (medial to inferior epigastric) vs indirect (lateral, through deep ring)
Femoral: below inguinal ligament, women, high obstruction risk
Umbilical, incisional, hiatal
Complications: irreducible, obstructed, strangulated (ischemia — emergency)
clinicalContext: Elderly patient with irreducible painful inguinal swelling 6 h, vomiting.
nursingPriority: NPO, IV fluids, NG tube, urgent surgical consult for strangulation — emergency herniotomy.

title: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
definition: Thrombus in deep vein, typically calf/thigh.
keyPoints: Virchow triad: venous stasis, endothelial injury, hypercoagulability
Signs: unilateral leg swelling, warmth, tenderness, Homan sign
Wells score to stratify
D-dimer sensitive not specific; Doppler USG confirms
Treatment: LMWH/DOAC/warfarin; IVC filter if anticoagulation contraindicated
pearls: Prophylaxis: LMWH + mechanical in all post-op.
clinicalContext: Post-op day 4 hip replacement with unilateral calf swelling.
nursingPriority: Doppler USG leg, start enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD pending, elevate leg, compression stocking, bedside PE assessment.

title: Osteomyelitis
definition: Bone infection, hematogenous or direct.
keyPoints: Commonest: S aureus (also MRSA)
Children: metaphysis long bones; adults: vertebrae
ESR, CRP elevated; MRI sensitive
Treatment: 4-6 wk IV antibiotics; surgical debridement for chronic
clinicalContext: 8-y-old with fever, limp, tender distal femur.
nursingPriority: Blood cultures x2, MRI, empiric anti-staph IV, ortho consult for drainage.

title: Rickets
definition: Defective mineralization of growing bone due to vit D/calcium/phosphate deficiency.
keyPoints: Signs: bowing legs (genu varum), rachitic rosary, Harrison sulcus, craniotabes, delayed fontanel closure
Labs: low calcium/phosphate, elevated ALP, low 25(OH)D
Treatment: vit D3 supplementation + calcium
clinicalContext: 2-y-old with bowed legs, delayed milestones, exclusively breastfed vegetarian mother.
nursingPriority: Send Ca/P/ALP/25(OH)D, start vit D3 60,000 IU weekly x6-8 wk + calcium, sunlight exposure, refer ortho if deformity.

title: Osteomalacia
definition: Adult equivalent of rickets — poor mineralization of osteoid.
keyPoints: Causes: vit D deficiency, chronic kidney disease, phosphate wasting
Signs: bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, waddling gait, Looser zones on X-ray
Treatment: vit D + calcium
clinicalContext: Elderly woman with diffuse bone pain and difficulty climbing stairs.
nursingPriority: Check 25(OH)D, Ca, P, ALP, start vit D3 60,000 IU weekly, calcium, fall prevention.

title: Fractures and healing
definition: Break in continuity of bone.
keyPoints: Types: complete/incomplete, open/closed, displaced, comminuted, greenstick (kids), stress
Healing: hematoma (0-7d) → fibrocartilaginous callus (2-3 wk) → bony callus (6-12 wk) → remodeling
Open fracture: irrigation, debridement, tetanus, antibiotics within 6 h
Fat embolism 12-72 h after long bone fracture: petechiae, hypoxia, confusion
clinicalContext: Long bone fracture patient 48 h post-injury develops dyspnea, petechiae on chest, confusion.
nursingPriority: Suspect fat embolism — high-flow O2, support ventilation, notify team; supportive care.

title: Local anesthesia
definition: Reversible nerve block.
keyPoints: Amides (no -caine echo): lidocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine
Esters: procaine, tetracaine — higher allergy risk
Max doses: lidocaine 4.5 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with adrenaline
Adrenaline prolongs action, reduces bleeding; avoid in end-arteries (finger, toe, penis, ear, nose)
Toxicity: CNS excitation → seizure → coma; cardiac arrest
clinicalContext: Hand laceration repair in 70 kg adult with 1% lidocaine.
nursingPriority: Max 4.5 mg/kg = 315 mg = 31.5 mL of 1%; avoid adrenaline in fingers, aspirate before injecting.

title: Surgical instruments — identification
definition: High-yield OR instruments.
keyPoints: Artery forceps: Spencer Wells, mosquito (mostly haemostasis)
Tissue forceps: Babcock (bowel), Allis (skin)
Needle holder: Mayo-Hegar, Crile-Wood
Retractors: Deaver, Balfour, Doyen (CS), Morris
Scissors: Mayo (heavy), Metzenbaum (fine dissection)
Clamps: Kocher (bowel), Satinsky (vascular)
clinicalContext: OSCE image of curved forceps with longitudinal serrations and transverse serrations at tip.
nursingPriority: Identify as Kocher artery forceps; used for bowel clamping/vascular control.

title: Basics of ventilator
definition: Mechanical ventilation modes and parameters.
keyPoints: Modes: CMV, AC, SIMV, PSV, CPAP, BiPAP
Settings: RR, Vt 6-8 mL/kg ideal body wt (ARDSNet), FiO2, PEEP 5-10, I:E 1:2
ARDS: low Vt (6 mL/kg), higher PEEP, plateau <30
Weaning: SBT on PSV, RSBI <105 suggests readiness
clinicalContext: ARDS patient on ventilator with Vt 500 mL for 70 kg (=7 mL/kg) not improving.
nursingPriority: Reduce Vt to 6 mL/kg (420), increase PEEP per ARDS table, monitor plateau pressure <30, prone if PaO2/FiO2 <150.

title: Achalasia cardia
definition: Failure of LES relaxation and absent esophageal peristalsis.
keyPoints: Dysphagia to solids AND liquids
Bird-beak on barium swallow
Manometry diagnostic — gold standard
Treatment: pneumatic dilation, Heller myotomy, POEM, botox injection
clinicalContext: Young adult with progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation.
nursingPriority: Refer for manometry, prepare for Heller myotomy/POEM, soft diet, head up after meals.

title: Zenker diverticulum
definition: Pharyngoesophageal pulsion diverticulum at Killian triangle.
keyPoints: Elderly, regurgitation of undigested food, halitosis, neck mass
Barium swallow diagnostic
Treatment: cricopharyngeal myotomy + diverticulectomy
clinicalContext: 75-y-old with regurgitation of undigested food hours after meals, halitosis.
nursingPriority: Refer for barium swallow and surgical evaluation.

title: GERD
definition: Reflux of gastric contents into esophagus.
keyPoints: Pyrosis, regurgitation, waterbrash, chronic cough, nocturnal asthma
Barrett esophagus complication
Diagnosis: pH monitoring, endoscopy
Lifestyle: weight loss, avoid late meals, head of bed elevation
Medical: PPI
Surgical: Nissen fundoplication for refractory
pearls: Alarm symptoms: dysphagia, weight loss, hematemesis, melena, anemia.
clinicalContext: 50-y-old with nocturnal retrosternal burning, sour taste.
nursingPriority: PPI (omeprazole) 20 mg OD before breakfast, weight loss, avoid late meals, head elevation; endoscopy if alarm symptoms.

title: Esophageal perforation
definition: Full-thickness tear; Boerhaave after vomiting (spontaneous).
keyPoints: Mackler triad: vomiting + chest pain + subcutaneous emphysema
Gastrografin swallow (not barium)
High mortality if not operated within 24 h
NPO, broad-spectrum antibiotics, surgical repair
clinicalContext: Post-endoscopy patient with chest pain, neck crepitus.
nursingPriority: NPO, IV fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, urgent CT with water-soluble contrast, surgical consult.

title: Barrett esophagus
definition: Metaplastic columnar epithelium replacing squamous in distal esophagus due to chronic GERD.
keyPoints: Risk of adenocarcinoma — surveillance endoscopy
Non-dysplastic: q3-5 y; low-grade dysplasia: q6-12 mo; high-grade: ablation
PPI long-term
clinicalContext: Chronic GERD patient, endoscopy shows salmon-colored mucosa distal esophagus.
nursingPriority: Biopsy to confirm metaplasia/dysplasia, continue PPI, schedule surveillance per dysplasia grade.

title: Infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis (IHPS)
definition: Hypertrophy of pyloric muscle causing gastric outlet obstruction in 4-6 wk-old infants.
keyPoints: Male >female (4:1), first-born, macrolide exposure
Projectile non-bilious vomiting; olive-shaped mass
Hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis (classic)
USG: pyloric muscle >3 mm thick, >15 mm length
Treatment: correct electrolytes first, then Ramstedt pyloromyotomy
clinicalContext: 6-wk-old boy with projectile non-bilious vomiting, olive mass RUQ.
nursingPriority: Correct hypochloremic alkalosis with IV NS + KCl before surgery; NG decompression; plan pyloromyotomy once pH and chloride normalized.

title: Peptic ulcer
definition: Gastric or duodenal mucosal break.
keyPoints: Duodenal: pain relieved by food, H pylori 90%
Gastric: pain worsened by food, H pylori 70%, risk of malignancy
Test: urea breath test, stool antigen, endoscopy + biopsy
Treatment: PPI + triple therapy (amoxicillin + clarithromycin) x14 d
Complications: bleed, perforation, obstruction
clinicalContext: H pylori + on UBT with epigastric pain.
nursingPriority: Start triple therapy: PPI BD + amoxicillin 1 g BD + clarithromycin 500 mg BD x14 d, confirm eradication UBT 4 wk after.

title: Portal hypertension
definition: Portal venous pressure >5 mmHg above IVC.
keyPoints: Causes: cirrhosis (commonest), portal vein thrombosis, schistosomiasis
Consequences: varices, splenomegaly, caput medusae, ascites, encephalopathy
Variceal bleed: terlipressin/octreotide, endoscopic band ligation, TIPSS
clinicalContext: Cirrhosis patient with hematemesis.
nursingPriority: Two large-bore IVs, crystalloid, blood cross-match, terlipressin IV, endoscopy for banding, prophylactic ceftriaxone.

title: Bariatric surgery
definition: Weight-loss surgery in BMI >40 or >35 with comorbidity.
keyPoints: Types: sleeve gastrectomy, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, adjustable band
Complications: anastomotic leak, dumping, B12/iron/Ca deficiency
Lifelong vitamin/mineral supplementation
clinicalContext: 45-y-old BMI 45 with T2DM post Roux-en-Y.
nursingPriority: Small frequent meals, chew thoroughly, lifelong multivitamin + B12 IM monthly, calcium, iron.

title: Meckel diverticulum
definition: True diverticulum of ileum — vitelline duct remnant.
keyPoints: Rule of 2s: 2% population, 2 ft from ileocecal valve, 2 inches long, 2% symptomatic, boys 2x, first 2 y of life
Painless rectal bleed (ectopic gastric mucosa)
Meckel scan (Tc-99m pertechnetate)
clinicalContext: 18-mo-old with painless rectal bleed.
nursingPriority: Meckel scan, prep for diverticulectomy if positive, stabilize with fluids and transfusion if needed.

title: Appendicitis
definition: Inflammation of vermiform appendix; commonest surgical abdomen.
keyPoints: Migration of pain to RIF, anorexia, low-grade fever, Rovsing/psoas/obturator signs, McBurney tenderness
Alvarado score >=7 = likely
USG/CT abdomen
Treatment: appendectomy (open or laparoscopic)
clinicalContext: 20-y-old with periumbilical pain migrating to RIF, anorexia, fever 38.
nursingPriority: NPO, IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics, urgent surgical consult for appendectomy.

title: Hemorrhoids
definition: Dilated anal cushions — internal above dentate, external below.
keyPoints: Internal grades: I (no prolapse), II (prolapse reduces spontaneously), III (manual reduction), IV (irreducible)
Painless bright red rectal bleed on defecation
High-fiber diet, sitz bath, warm water, analgesics
Rubber band ligation (grade I-II), sclerotherapy, hemorrhoidectomy (grade III-IV)
clinicalContext: 40-y-old with painless bright red rectal bleed on defecation, grade II.
nursingPriority: High-fiber diet, stool softener, sitz bath, refer for rubber band ligation.

title: Anal fissure
definition: Linear tear in anoderm distal to dentate line.
keyPoints: Posterior midline 90%; other locations suspect IBD/TB
Severe pain on defecation, bright red bleed, sentinel tag, hypertrophied papilla
Treatment: sitz bath, high-fiber, GTN ointment, botulinum toxin, lateral sphincterotomy
clinicalContext: Patient with severe tearing anal pain on defecation, small bleed.
nursingPriority: Sitz bath, high-fiber diet, 0.4% GTN ointment BD, analgesia, refer if not healed in 6 wk.

title: Colorectal cancer
definition: Adenocarcinoma of colon/rectum.
keyPoints: Risk: FAP, HNPCC, UC, low-fiber/high-red meat, smoking
Symptoms: change in bowel habit, bleeding, tenesmus, iron-deficiency anemia
Screening: FIT/FOBT from 50 y, colonoscopy q10 y
Staging: TNM; Dukes A-D
Surgery ± chemo ± radiation
clinicalContext: 55-y-old with change in bowel habit and iron-def anemia.
nursingPriority: Colonoscopy + biopsy, CT for staging, refer to oncology/surgery.

title: Massive blood transfusion protocol
definition: Replacement of >=10 units RBC in 24 h or >=4 units in 1 h.
keyPoints: 1:1:1 PRBC:FFP:Platelet ratio
Complications: hypothermia, hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia (citrate), acidosis, TRALI, TACO
Monitor coagulation, ionized calcium, temperature
Warm blood, give calcium gluconate per 4 U
clinicalContext: Trauma patient requiring 8 units PRBC in 30 min.
nursingPriority: Activate MTP, maintain 1:1:1 ratio, warm blood, calcium gluconate 1 g IV per 4 U, monitor potassium and pH.

title: Triage — START and disaster
definition: Sorting casualties by urgency.
keyPoints: START (adult): assess Respirations, Perfusion, Mental status
Tags: Red (immediate), Yellow (delayed), Green (minor/walking wounded), Black (expectant/deceased)
JumpSTART for pediatric
ED triage: ESI 1-5 or Manchester
clinicalContext: Mass casualty with 30 victims; you are first responder.
nursingPriority: Call walking wounded to one area (Green), then check respirations — if absent after airway opened = Black; RR >30 or perfusion capillary refill >2 s or altered mental = Red; others = Yellow.
